claim: As of October 2026, Claude Code's permission system lets an organization control what it does without asking: in Manual mode it starts read-only and asks before editing files or running commands, unmatched commands need approval, file reads inside the working directory do not prompt, and rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow. Auto mode, where a separate classifier model reviews actions, is the built-in starting mode for interactive terminal sessions, and administrators can set the starting mode and disable auto and bypass modes in managed settings.

sources.title: Claude Code docs: Security (Permission-based architecture)
sources.excerpt: Manual mode: Claude Code starts with read-only permissions. When it needs to edit files, run tests, or execute commands, it asks you first. ... Auto mode is the built-in starting permission mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions. File reads, Grep: no approval required within the working directory and additional directories (Permissions table).

sources.title: Claude Code docs: Permissions
sources.excerpt: Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. ... To prevent bypassPermissions or auto mode from being used, set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode or permissions.disableAutoMode to 'disable' ... most useful in managed settings where they can't be overridden.

notes: Do not say 'it always asks first': the documented default starting mode is Auto, which delegates some approvals to a classifier; the organization chooses the starting mode. Bash deny and ask rules match the command text and are not a security boundary around a program (the permissions page says so); pair them with the sandbox for OS-level enforcement. The security page states the user is responsible for reviewing proposed code and commands.

claim: Claude Code includes an optional sandbox for shell commands, enforced by the operating system (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2), that limits which files they can write and which network domains they can reach; it is off by default, administrators can require it through managed settings, and it covers shell commands only, so file tools, MCP servers and hooks run outside it and, by default, sandboxed commands can still read most of the machine including credential files unless an administrator denies those paths.

sources.title: Claude Code docs: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool
sources.excerpt: The Bash sandbox is a boundary that the operating system enforces around the shell commands Claude runs on your machine. ... The sandbox is off by default. ... The sandbox covers shell commands only. Claude's file tools, MCP servers, and hooks run outside it.

notes: Network default: no direct route out; connections go through a local proxy that checks each host against allowed domains, which start empty. Reads default: most of the machine, including ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials, changeable with filesystem.denyRead and credentials settings. On native Windows, commands run unsandboxed; by default Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed if the sandbox cannot start, unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable is true. Enforcement in managed settings: sandbox.enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false, allowManagedDomainsOnly. For stronger isolation the docs suggest running the whole process in a container or VM.

claim: Claude Code's documented safeguards against prompt injection include permission prompts for sensitive operations, no automatic approval of network fetch commands such as curl and wget, detection of commands it cannot fully analyze, fail-closed matching of unrecognised commands, and a separate model call that summarizes fetched web pages; Anthropic's documentation also states that no system is completely immune to all attacks.

sources.title: Claude Code docs: Security (Protect against prompt injection)
sources.excerpt: While these protections significantly reduce risk, no system is completely immune to all attacks. Always maintain good security practices when working with any AI tool.

notes: The safeguards named in Manual mode: network request approval, web page summaries via a separate model call, trust verification of folders and .mcp.json servers, command injection detection, fail-closed matching, secure credential storage. Best practices listed: review commands before approval, avoid piping untrusted content directly to Claude, verify changes to critical files, use VMs for scripts that touch external services. Never claim prompt injection is solved.

claim: Administrators can deploy managed settings through the claude.ai admin console (Teams and Enterprise), device management policy, or a file on disk; they sit above user and project settings and can lock permission rules, disable bypass and auto permission modes, require the sandbox, restrict MCP servers, hooks, models and providers, require login to the company's own organization, and load an organization-wide CLAUDE.md that cannot be excluded. Developers can extend managed permission lists but not remove from them.

notes: Named keys: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, permissions.disableAutoMode, permissions.defaultMode, sandbox.enabled, allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, forceLoginMethod, forceLoginOrgUUID, allowedProviders (newer versions), availableModels with enforceAvailableModels. claim: As of October 2026, Anthropic's glossary defines agentic coding as a workflow where the AI can read files, run commands and make changes autonomously while you watch, redirect or step away, as opposed to chat-based assistants that only respond with text you must apply yourself. Claude Code works in a loop of gathering context, taking action and verifying results. Plan mode (entered with Shift+Tab or /plan) lets Claude research and propose changes without editing source files. Non-interactive mode (claude -p, formerly called headless mode) runs a single prompt and exits, for CI and scripts. A hook is a user-defined handler that runs automatically at a fixed point in Claude Code's lifecycle, deterministically rather than at the model's discretion. A subagent is a specialized assistant with its own context window, tools and permissions that returns a summary. MCP is an open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources and services.
